title: StratusData POC capacity & autoscale scoping
summary: Kickoff scoping call for a 4-week POC to validate inference economics and latency for StratusData's batch+interactive workloads. Discussed target SLOs, baseline traffic shape, reserved GPU sizing, autoscaling thresholds, burst capacity to on-demand, and fallback to quantized / smaller model variants. Agreed next steps: share sample prompts and traces, Redwood to provision test pool & run benchmark, pricing and sizing sheet to be sent, schedule benchmark run next Wednesday.
action_items: Alex Chen: send pricing + reserved capacity sizing spreadsheet (due 2025-03-07)
Priya Patel: provision test GPU pool and run Redwood benchmark scripts, share results (due 2025-03-12)
Elena Gomez: upload representative prompt set, traffic traces, and token distribution (due 2025-03-06)
Samir Das: confirm network egress and VPC peering constraints; provide security contact (due 2025-03-10)
next_steps: Redwood to provision 2x A10 reserved GPUs for baseline + allow burst to 4x on-demand during benchmark
Customer to provide 48 hours of representative traces and sample prompts
Schedule live benchmark run (Priya + Elena) for 2025-03-12
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark results and sizing recommendations within 3 business days of run
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (StratusData CTO), Elena Gomez (StratusData ML Eng), Samir Das (StratusData Infra), Hannah Li (Product)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - Alex from Redwood, Priya and Jordan here on the infra side, and from StratusData I think Mark, Elena, Samir and Hannah are on. Can you all hear me okay?
[00:10] Mark Rivera: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Alex. We wanted to scope a POC to validate latency and unit cost for our interactive search plus batch embedding workload.
[00:20] Alex Chen: Perfect. High-level goal for Redwood today is to size reserved GPUs for the POC and define autoscale & burst strategy so you can hit a realistic SLO while controlling spend.
[00:35] Priya Patel: Quick note - we often recommend a small reserved pool for baseline throughput and then allow burst to on-demand instances for spikes; fallback policies to smaller quantized variants if latency targets can't be met. But we'll tailor to your traffic.
[00:50] Elena Gomez: Our workload is about 40% interactive chat/search, 60% offline batch embeddings. Interactive peak is roughly 60 QPS with 1.2k token average per request; batch runs at night ~2M tokens per hour.
[01:10] Jordan Lee: Thanks, Elena. Couple clarifying q's: those 60 QPS peak, is that sustained for minutes or short spikes?
[01:18] Elena Gomez: Usually spikes last 2-8 minutes tied to product releases; typical plateau is around 20-25 QPS daytime.
[01:26] Samir Das: Also note we have strict egress limits from our VPC; can't exceed certain outgoing bandwidth during business hours - that's why burst planning matters.
[01:36] Priya Patel: Understood. For a POC we suggest provisioning a reserved pool sized to handle the daytime plateau - say 2x A10s to start - and allow burst to 2 additional on-demand units for short spikes. That gets us coverage for ~30-40 QPS steady and up to ~60 QPS with burst depending on model choice and batching.
[01:56] Mark Rivera: That sounds reasonable. What's the fallback if burst capacity isn't available? We need an option that keeps UX acceptable.
[02:05] Alex Chen: Two levers: 1) automatic model fallback - route to a quantized variant or smaller architecture with slightly higher error but much lower latency/cost; 2) degrade gracefully - return cached responses for common prefixes, or use prefix/KV caching for repeated queries. Also you can set hard concurrency limits per customer to shape latency.
[02:28] Elena Gomez: Quick question - how much performance delta do you see between a 16-bit model on A10 vs an 8-bit quantized one? Ballpark numbers?
[02:36] Priya Patel: Ballpark: quantized 8-bit can reduce memory footprint by ~40-50% and inference latency per token is often 1.2-1.6x faster depending on kernel optimizations; but quality can drop slightly for edge cases. We'll include side-by-side metrics in the bench run.
[02:55] Mark Rivera: Okay. For success criteria I'd say: p50 latency < 200ms for interactive flows, p95 < 600ms; throughput to support 60 QPS bursts without >1% error rate; cost per 1M tokens under our target. Also audit logs and SSO integration must be demonstrated.
[03:20] Alex Chen: Sounds good - we can codify those. For the POC scope we usually: baseline run to measure single-node perf; stress run with reserved + burst; fallback scenario where we intentionally remove on-demand burst to validate degraded path; and cost calc. Timeline typical is 2 weeks for baseline + 2 weeks for extended runs - total ~4 weeks.
[03:40] Hannah Li: We have internal stakeholder deadline end of April, so 4 weeks fits if we start ASAP.
[03:47] Samir Das: Security checks - we'll need SOC2 docs and SAML metadata for SSO; Priya, do you need anything else on infra side?
[03:56] Priya Patel: We'll need an account for the test cluster, network IPs for VPC peering, and ideally a sample dataset and 48 hours of traces. Also note that if you want Private deployment (VPC), some features like burst to Redwood-hosted on-demand require cross-account agreements - we'll outline options.
[04:18] Mark Rivera: For the POC can we do Private VPC? We prefer to test in our VPC to validate egress.
[04:24] Jordan Lee: We can do a Private deployment for the POC with a customer-managed VPC; for burst to Redwood-hosted capacity we can either route via secure peering or implement a fallback where excess load is queued or served by smaller local variants. There are tradeoffs: peering adds setup time and approvals.
[04:45] Elena Gomez: If peering takes too long can we at least run an in-our-VPC baseline and then a separate hosted burst run?
[04:53] Priya Patel: Yes - many customers do a hybrid test: baseline in your VPC, then a controlled hosted burst run to measure differences. We'll coordinate the bench windows to respect your egress limits.
[05:05] Mark Rivera: Great. On sizing - you recommended 2x A10 reserved. Can you share expected QPS per GPU for our model family? We're evaluating an Llama2-like 13B and a smaller 7B variant for fallback.
[05:18] Priya Patel: For a 13B on A10 with our optimized kernels and typical 1.2k tokens, a single A10 might sustain ~12-18 interactive QPS with low latency when using batching and KV cache. So 2 A10s ~24-36 steady QPS. For 7B you can expect ~30-50 QPS per A10. We'll validate in bench.
[05:40] Elena Gomez: That delta is helpful; so fallback to 7B could be primary strategy for heavy spikes. How about embedding batch throughput?
[05:48] Jordan Lee: Embedding is much more IO-bound; for batch embedding throughput we usually recommend separate worker nodes sized for throughput - those are cheaper per token. For 2M tokens/hour at night we can schedule batch slots to keep reserved capacity cheaper.
[06:02] Samir Das: Are there automation knobs for autoscale - like thresholds, cooldowns, and max burst?
[06:08] Priya Patel: Yes - autoscale policies include CPU/GPU utilization thresholds, queue length thresholds, and token-per-second thresholds. We recommend a conservative cooldown of 60-120s for GPU spin-ups and a max burst cap to control spend. For short spikes we prefer burst to on-demand instead of immediate scale-out, combined with request queuing for slightly longer events.
[06:30] Mark Rivera: Any fallback policy suggestions to guarantee <1% errors during spikes?
[06:35] Alex Chen: A layered approach: 1) soft-failover to quantized model; 2) priority routing for authenticated users; 3) circuit breaker that returns cached/approximate answers for known high-frequency queries; 4) degrade to synchronous batch response for non-critical flows. We'll demo these in the stress test.
[06:55] Elena Gomez: For the bench we'll want to run: cold start latency, steady-state p50/p95, burst stress to 120% of expected peak, and fallback path - makes sense?
[07:03] Priya Patel: Yes - that's our typical checklist. We'll run both 13B and 7B variants and a quantized 7B-8bit.
[07:10] Mark Rivera: About cost - can you provide an estimated monthly cost for reserved 2x A10 plus on-demand burst assumptions?
[07:18] Alex Chen: We'll send a sizing + pricing sheet. For the POC we can also offer a time-boxed discount or trial credits to reduce trial cost - I'll include that.
[07:26] Hannah Li: From product side we also want metrics in the console: per-route latency, token costs, per-token attribution. Can we get demo dashboard?
[07:33] Jordan Lee: Yes - Redwood Console will show token-level cost, per-route latency, and can trace requests. We'll share a short recording of the dashboard and the route-level view.
[07:44] Samir Das: Security - SAML, audit logs, KMS integration for keys. We'll need to validate these before any Private deployment sign-off.
[07:54] Priya Patel: We have docs for SOC2, SAML, KMS, and audit logs. I'll attach those. For KMS there are supported HSM integrations as well.
[08:03] Mark Rivera: Good. What's the estimated time to provision the reserved pool and run the initial benchmark?
[08:09] Priya Patel: If we get traces and sample prompts by Thursday (2025-03-06), we can provision the pool and run baseline tests by Wednesday (2025-03-12). Full POC runs through end of March / early April.
[08:23] Elena Gomez: Sounds doable. We'll aim to upload traces today or tomorrow.
[08:29] Alex Chen: Great. Any other open concerns?
[08:33] Mark Rivera: One last thing - do you support canary rollouts for model changes during POC? We may want to test two model versions A/B.
[08:41] Jordan Lee: Yes - Redwood supports canary rollouts and A/B routing. You can pin routes to model versions and we can run traffic splits during the bench to measure regressions.
[08:51] Priya Patel: We'll also enable quality monitoring to detect regressions against your eval prompts automatically.
[08:58] Hannah Li: Perfect.
[09:00] Alex Chen: Ok I'll recap next steps: Alex to send pricing + sizing sheet by 2025-03-07; Priya to provision test pool and run bench 2025-03-12; Elena to provide traces/prompts by 2025-03-06; Samir to share security contact & VPC details by 2025-03-10. We'll schedule a follow-up after bench. Any objections?
[09:20] Mark Rivera: No objections. Thanks everyone.
[09:25] Elena Gomez: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:28] Alex Chen: Thanks all - we'll follow up in email with links to docs and the sizing sheet.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" in automated notes), speaker labels may be generic in parts. References: Redwood Console screenshot link (shared in chat), sizing spreadsheet (to be sent), SOC2 + SAML docs (Priya to attach).
